title: Compact delta snapshots and runbook suggester for first responders
author: Maya Kapoor
description:
Motivation: On-call responders frequently need a compact, machine-readable comparison between two incident telemetry snapshots (pre- and post-mitigation) and a prioritized set of suggested runbook steps. This PR introduces a compact delta snapshot format (top N metric deltas + representative traces + signal-level diffs) and a lightweight runbook suggester that maps fingerprinted telemetry deltas to curated runbook templates. The goal is to reduce mean-time-to-resolution by surfacing the smallest actionable delta and a short, ranked action list.

What this change does: Adds a server-side delta generator that collapses metrics/traces into a human-friendly unified diff, an HTTP API and incidentctl CLI command to fetch diffs, and a recommendation engine that returns 1-3 prioritized runbook actions with confidence scores. The feature is gated behind the feature flag `incident_delta_v1` and a sampling rollout keyed by org id.

Design notes: The delta format focuses on three sections: 1) Metric deltas (relative + absolute, with top contributors), 2) Trace exemplars (one per high-impact span group, with safe redaction), 3) Config/route changes detected via config hash comparisons. Runbook suggestions are produced by a rule engine: fingerprint match -> template scoring -> post-filter (safety checks and PII scrub). The engine is intentionally rule-first to keep explainability and auditability in playbooks.

API/CLI: New endpoints: POST /incidents/:id/snapshots/diff (body: {from_snapshot,to_snapshot,options}) and GET /incidents/:id/runbook-suggest. CLI: `incidentctl snapshot diff --from <id> --to <id>` and `incidentctl suggest --incident <id>`. Outputs include a short text summary and a compact machine diff (JSON) for programmatic consumption.

Testing and QA: Unit tests cover delta generation logic, redaction, and the template scoring heuristics. E2E tests simulate a noisy production-like workload and assert prioritization stability. Load tests show the delta generation path adds ~12ms p99 at 50 QPS when sample_size=10. CI initially showed a flaky integration test (tests/e2e/oncall_snapshot_diff.test.ts) which was fixed by increasing mocked trace timeouts.

Rollout plan: Feature gated and gradually enabled for 5% of orgs for the first 48 hours, then 25% after monitoring. Telemetry events added: incident.delta.request, incident.delta.size, incident.runbook.suggest which feed into the oncall metrics dashboard. A short monitoring playbook is included to automatically rollback the flag if error rates or latency regressions exceed thresholds.

Docs and migration: Adds a docs page describing the diff format and CLI usage. No data migration is required. Backwards compatibility: existing snapshot APIs are unchanged; the new endpoints are additive.

release_notes: Introduce compact incident delta snapshots and a machine-assisted runbook suggester behind feature flag incident_delta_v1. Adds CLI and API endpoints, new observability events, and docs. Feature gated and non-breaking.
